strings.name: Mike Henry
strings.role: Former BHP CEO and Executive Director
strings.country: Born in Canada; career mainly in Australia
strings.summary: Mike Henry is a Canadian-born mining executive who gained commercial and operational experience at Mitsubishi Corporation and BHP before leading BHP for six and a half years. During his tenure, the company merged its petroleum business with Woodside and acquired OZ Minerals, while also pursuing an unsuccessful attempt to acquire Anglo American. He handed over his CEO and board responsibilities at the end of June 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 17 November 2026. Distinguishes retirement as CEO and director from the continuing employment transition, and transaction announcements from completion and uncompleted proposals; birth is recorded only to the year given by a secondary source.
strings.influence.rationale: Led BHP, participating in global mining portfolio adjustments and the supply of resources needed for the energy transition.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education and early career
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned a BSc in Chemistry from the University of British Columbia; worked at Mitsubishi Corporation, was seconded to BMA in 2001 and joined BHP permanently in 2003.
strings.facts.f2.label: Retirement and transition
strings.facts.f2.value: His CEO and board tenure ended on 30 June 2026, with Brandon Craig succeeding him on 1 July; the company arranged for him to provide support until 30 November.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Reshaping mining assets
strings.highlights.h1.text: During his tenure, the petroleum business merged with Woodside and the OZ Minerals acquisition added copper and nickel resources, as group-level portfolio changes.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Commercial and operational experience
strings.highlights.h2.text: Moved from coal business development and marketing into Australian mining operations before becoming group CEO.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Retiring as CEO and director
strings.timeline.t1.text: Ended a six-and-a-half-year tenure; his successor took office the next day, and transition support did not mean continuing as CEO.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Participating in the half-year results Q&A
strings.timeline.t2.text: Discussed results for the period ended December 2025 and capital allocation; copper production guidance remained a forecast.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Ending that round of the Anglo American acquisition attempt
strings.timeline.t3.text: BHP announced it would not make a firm offer; that proposal did not result in a completed acquisition.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Completing the OZ Minerals acquisition
strings.timeline.t4.text: BHP acquired all OZ Minerals shares through a wholly owned subsidiary.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Petroleum business merges with Woodside
strings.timeline.t5.text: The group completed the petroleum merger and distributed Woodside shares to shareholders as an in-specie dividend.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becoming BHP CEO
strings.timeline.t6.text: Succeeded Andrew Mackenzie, with the effective appointment date distinct from the earlier announcement.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Leading Australian minerals operations
strings.timeline.t7.text: Became President Operations, Minerals Australia, responsible for the local iron ore, coal, copper and nickel businesses.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joining BHP permanently
strings.timeline.t8.text: After a business development secondment to BMA, took roles at BHP including coal business development.
